svg.title: For the first inequality, separate the uniform small input ut from the plotted nonnegative excess. The wide column bound costs aL2 on the small input, while the row bound a/L2 multiplies the total excess, at most 2u P E. Thus the large-input term retains its L−2 saving. The noise argument uses narrow row and column bounds a, and the coarse argument uses the plotted excess bound directly. In each case the stencil radius takes the tested two-radius dome into the input three- or five-radius dome, so only the given local split is used.
